gaps.sentence: A sales rep will follow ___ your enquiry next week.
gaps.explanation: follow up = take further action after something.

gaps.sentence: The plane will drop ___ the parcels at the next farm.
gaps.explanation: drop off = deliver somebody/something; also become less (sales dropped off).

gaps.sentence: I can't make ___ what the sign says from here.
gaps.explanation: make out = see, hear or understand with difficulty.

gaps.sentence: The police are cracking ___ on unlicensed street vendors.
gaps.explanation: 'Crack down on' = deal firmly with illegal behaviour.

gaps.sentence: He stole the pens and got away ___ it.
gaps.explanation: get away with something = do wrong without being punished.

gaps.sentence: Feel free to drop ___ for a coffee any time.
gaps.explanation: drop in = pay a casual visit; drop off = fall asleep or deliver.

gaps.sentence: Wake ___ — you'll be late for school!
Everyone says she takes ___ her grandmother.
gaps.explanation: take after a relative = resemble them in character/looks.
